text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH — kubelet NotReady spike detected in inference-usw-1 pool (multiple restarts). Auto-escalation to on-call.
alex: seeing a swarm of NotReady events across 3 nodes in infer-usw-1, started ~05:12 UTC. Affected pods showing CrashLoopBackOff and some 502s from the gateway.
maya: logs show kubelet restarted on node infer-usw-1a-07 twice in last 6m. dmesg has GPU reset lines and a bunch of 'kworker' OOM killers.
alex: running quick check: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer-usw-1
alex: ```
infer-usw-1a-07   NotReady   <none>   120m   v1.26.3   10.2.1.7   gpu:tesla-v100
infer-usw-1a-08   Ready      <none>   14d    v1.26.3   10.2.1.8   gpu:tesla-v100
infer-usw-1a-09   NotReady   <none>   2m     v1.26.3   10.2.1.9   gpu:tesla-v100
``` 
maya: kubelet logs show repeated segfaults in cri runtime after driver reset. suspect GPU driver/firmware loop.
infra-bot: Alert: 12% of inference-hosted requests in us-west show increased latency > 800ms, 3% 502 errors.
alex: impact looks customer-facing for heavy-gen jobs. CS notified.
cs-rep: getting reports from a few enterprise customers about timeouts on long generation requests, asking for ETA.
maya: mitigation plan — 1) cordon the two NotReady nodes, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) scale up spare dedicated pool in eu-west as temporary capacity, 4) enable fallback routing for hosted API to smaller model variants.
samantha: I'm on-call next, taking handoff. Steps I'll run now:
- cordon infer-usw-1a-07
- drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data infer-usw-1a-07
- add 4 nodes to dedicated-infer-usw pool
samantha: cordon + drain started on infer-usw-1a-07 (05:21 UTC)
alex: while draining, noticed runtime on some pods failing with CUDA error: 'device-side assert' in logs — those are likely from the model runtime hitting kernel issues during restart.
maya: quick hotfix: enable nodeSelector to steer new pods to infer-usw-1a-08 and to eu-west while we evaluate driver state.
alex: command to scale dedicated pool (runbook):
```bash
rctl scale pool dedicated-infer-usw --replicas 8 --region eu-west-1
``` 
infra-bot: autoscaler request accepted, provisioning 4 nodes in eu-west-1 (ETA ~6m).
samantha: drain done on infer-usw-1a-07, cordoned. Starting kernel driver check -> ssh node and capture /var/log/kern.log and nvidia-smi output.
samantha: nvidia-smi shows GPU 0 reset count incrementing and one GPU in 'Unknown' state.
maya: ask infra to bump evict thresholds so scheduler doesn't immediately pack onto flaky nodes.
ops-lead: also enable fallback routing in the edge proxy for customers with >1s SLOs; push config toggle now.
alex: toggled fallback routing to smaller model for experimental customers (05:33 UTC) — should reduce long-running jobs hitting flaky nodes.
cs-rep: updating affected customers: "We're investigating an infrastructure issue in us-west affecting long generation jobs; traffic is being routed to other regions, ETA 30m." Can we confirm ETA?
infra-bot: eu-west nodes ready and registered (05:38 UTC). Traffic shifting 7% to eu-west dedicated pool.
samantha: still seeing node infer-usw-1a-09 flapping; repeating kubelet restart every ~90s. Suspect kernel/GPU driver race on shutdown path.
alex: next steps: 1) isolate these nodes from scheduling until we repro driver issue, 2) collect core dumps and kernel OOPS, 3) coordinate driver rollback or kernel patch with infra.
maya: collecting coredumps now, uploading to s3://redwood-internal/incident/3290012345/
ops-lead: temporary mitigation complete: traffic rerouted, eu-west capacity added, cordoned nodes drained. Customer impact reduced to ~1% errors.
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation in progress — customer impact reduced. Severity: HIGH -> ACTIVE (no longer P1). Next update in 30m or on significant change.
samantha: handing off to maya for post-mortem and driver patch runway. I'll remain available if nodes flapping again.
maya: acknowledged, will open a postmortem ticket and link logs. Initial hypothesis: recent NVIDIA driver push + kernel update caused regression under heavy load causing kubelet to crash when waiting on device resets.
alex: notes for postmortem: timestamped kubelet logs, nvidia-smi resets, docker/CRI logs, pod runtime stack traces. Add list of affected customer IDs and request IDs (CS will provide).
cs-rep: I'll send a customer impact summary and who was notified.
ops-lead: once stable, we should uncordon nodes only after driver rollback or validated kernel fix and at least 1h of stable telemetry.
maya: creating postmortem ticket: PM-3290012345 and assigning to eng-ml + infra teams.
incident-bot: Incident closed? No — moving to monitoring. Last action at 3290012600 UTC.
